core_obligations: Spread the condition on E off X_1 to an open U and write the localized class of E through the complement Z of U using the shrink lemma (proof lines 10986-10998).
Verify the two defining compositions: vanishing against i_{1,*} because X_1 cap Z is empty, and the identification against i_{2,*} giving P_p(E_2) or c_p(E_2) (proof lines 11000-11009).
proof_roadmap: The open neighbourhood U and the complement Z (proof lines 10986-10992).
Shrinking the support of the localized class (proof lines 10994-10998).
The two compositions and conclusion (proof lines 11000-11009).
difficulty_reason: In the setting of Lemma labelled lemma-silly, if E_2 is the restriction of a perfect E in D(O_X) whose restriction to X_1 is zero, resp. finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0, and E satisfies assumption (3) of Situation labelled situation-loc-chern, then the class P'_p(E_2), resp. c'_p(E_2), agrees with P_p(X_2 -> X, E), resp. c_p(X_2 -> X, E) (statement lines 10974-10984). The proof first spreads the condition to an open: the assumptions on E give an open U containing X_1 over which E is zero or finite locally free of rank < p, by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field (proof lines 10986-10992). With Z the complement of U carrying the reduced induced structure, Lemma labelled lemma-loc-chern-shrink-Z gives P_p(X_2 -> X, E) = (Z -> X_2)_* o P_p(Z -> X, E) and the same for c_p (proof lines 10994-10998). It remains to verify the characterisation of P'_p(E_2) from Lemma labelled lemma-silly: because X_1 cap Z is empty, Lemma labelled lemma-loc-chern-disjoint makes the composition with i_{1,*} vanish, while Lemma labelled lemma-loc-chern-after-pushforward gives that the composition with i_{2,*} is P_p(E_2), which pins the class down (proof lines 11000-11009). Spreading the vanishing off X_1 to an open neighbourhood and then testing the two defining compositions is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
